inventory.content: O(n) is the real matrix group O^T O = I.
Full O(n) is equipped with Haar probability measure.
O(n) has the two determinant components det O = +1 and det O = -1.
Each determinant component has full-Haar probability 1/2.
For b in {-1,+1}, mu_{n,b} is full Haar conditioned on det O = b.
kappa >= 4 and n >= 3 are the single-block parameter restrictions.
n <= d and k = floor(d/n) define ambient dimension and number of blocks.
inventory.reason: No d or block count occurs in the current single-block theorem.

inventory.content: The main proof chooses n = 2T+1 for query budget T, under T >= 1 and 2T+1 <= d; remaining cases are separate.
inventory.reason: Algorithm/query-budget specialization and exceptional cases belong to the later lower-bound argument.

inventory.content: Eq4 defines A_O = ((kappa+1)/2)I - ((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T).
Eq5 defines block-diagonal A_boldO, with an identity remainder block.
inventory.reason: The proposed statement has no block-product precision.

inventory.content: For each b, draw k orthogonal matrices independently from mu_{n,b}.
inventory.reason: Product-prior sampling is outside construction of a single-block mixture.

inventory.content: D_b is the law of the resulting block precision; all blocks share sign b.
inventory.reason: The ambient hard-input distribution and shared-sign block construction are not conclusions or premises of this packet.

inventory.content: P_b = E_{O~mu_{n,b}}[N(0,A_O^{-1})] is the single-block target mixture.
Eq6 identifies the averaged ambient target with P_b tensor-power k times N(0,I_{d-kn}).
inventory.reason: Block independence and Gaussian product factorization require a distinct theorem.

inventory.reason: Zero-remainder block convention is irrelevant to the single-block theorem.

inventory.content: The single-block mixtures will be separated by a bounded radial test.
Separation will then be amplified across independent blocks.
inventory.reason: Amplification lies beyond the present single-block mixture construction.

inventory.content: The single-block calculation combines Gaussian-normalization cancellation with two spherical Poisson identities.
inventory.reason: These analytic identities and quantitative separation are not supplied as proof steps for measurability or bind well-definedness.

inventory.content: The section again fixes n >= 3 and kappa >= 4 and uses O Haar on full O(n).

inventory.content: p_O denotes the density of N(0,A_O^{-1}).
p_b denotes the density of P_b for each sign.
For lambda >= 0, h_lambda(x) = exp(-lambda ||x||^2).
H(lambda) = E_fullHaar[det(O) integral h_lambda(x) p_O(x) dx].
Using equal determinant-component masses, H(lambda) = (E_{P_+1} h_lambda - E_{P_-1} h_lambda)/2.
For lambda >= 0, 0 < h_lambda <= 1.
The authors next compute H(lambda) and choose lambda > 0.
inventory.reason: This announces later quantitative work; the supplied regions contain neither computation nor choice, and the current theorem asserts neither.

source_gap_nodes.detail: No supplied source region proves that O -> N(0,A_O^{-1}) is a measurable map into Borel measures. This is a required formal producer, not an author-provided proof step.
The expectation notation defining P_b omits construction as bind, probability preservation and evaluation on arbitrary Borel sets. These are precisely the proposed packet's added bookkeeping.

The supplied regions define the inverse-precision Gaussian but do not prove SPD of A_O. The seal claims an existing exact law/density parent; that claim was not independently inspected, and no SPD proof is attributed to these regions.

The source uses p_b and the H expectation identity without supplying the measure-to-density and integral interchange justification in these regions. Those additional obligations belong to later bridges, not to a claimed author proof of the current theorem.
